labelReview.scope: Neuralink N1/R1 research program: skull-mounted electronics, intracortical recording threads and software-mediated external device control. Public study and sponsor sources; not a commercial IFU.
models: PRIME sponsor brochure (revision not established): 64 threads / 1,024 electrodes
UCLH GB-PRIME description (31 July 2025): 128 threads / 1,024 electrodes
2019 platform prototype (not equivalent to current clinical N1)

findings.text: Neuralink describes its devices as investigational and not FDA approved. Study permission and an IDE are not marketing authorization.
The PRIME registry describes a skull-mounted N1 connected to implanted brain threads. R1 inserts those threads and is not the chronic implant.
findings.locator: Brief summary; interventions; study status and outcomes

findings.text: The undated sponsor brochure describes 64 threads and 1,024 electrodes. The PDF revision and configuration used in every participant are not established.
findings.locator: PDF p. 1; devices and study purpose

findings.text: UCLH reports 128 threads with eight electrodes each in its 2025 GB-PRIME description. The thread count differs from the sponsor brochure, despite the same total electrode count.
The sponsor reported thread retraction and fewer effective electrodes in an early participant. This is a manufacturer report, not an FDA recall determination or a cohort-wide event rate.
The 2019 platform paper predates PRIME and describes an earlier preclinical platform. It is not evidence of the current N1 human studies’ results.
findings.locator: Device description and animal experiments; distinct from N1 human study results

The N1 Implant is a skull-mounted, wireless, rechargeable implant connected to electrode threads that are implanted in the brain by the R1 Robot, a robotic electrode thread inserter.

researchEvidence.title: Control of Assistive Devices Via Brain-Computer Interface Technology

interventions.description: The intervention involves using the N1 Implant, a wireless brain-computer interface (BCI), to enable participants to control the Assistive Robotic Arm through neural signals.
interventions.name: Assistive Robotic Arm

researchEvidence.summary: The CONVOY Study is a clinical trial designed to explore the feasibility of participants from the PRIME Study (NCT06429735) using the N1 Implant to control various assistive devices. The main goal is to determine whether participants can successfully modulate their brain activity to control devices, such as an Assistive Robotic Arm (ARA). This study will assess the effectiveness, consistency, and safety of neural control using the ARA and other assistive devices.

primaryOutcomes.measure: Ability of participants to modulate brain activity for controlling an assistive device via the N1 Implant.
primaryOutcomes.timeFrame: 3-months following first use of the assistive device

researchEvidence.summary: The CAN-PRIME Study is to test the safety and functionality of Neuralink's N1 Implant and R1 Robot in people who have difficulty moving their arms and legs (tetraparesis or tetraplegia). The N1 Implant is a small, wireless device placed in the skull. It connects to tiny threads inserted into the brain by the R1 Robot, which is a machine designed to carefully place these threads. This study will help researchers learn how well the implant and robot work and if they are safe for use.

The N1 Implant is a wireless, rechargeable device mounted on the skull, connected to electrode threads that are inserted into the brain by the R1 Robot, which is a robotic device specifically designed for this procedure.

researchEvidence.summary: The VOICE Study is an early feasibility study to evaluate the initial clinical safety and efficacy of the N1 and R1 Systems device design concept in providing an ability to communicate. The Neuralink N1 Implant is intended to provide the ability to communicate to individuals with severe and irreversible speech production impairment. It is indicated for adults with neurological conditions of the central speech pathways who have impaired upper limb function. The N1 Implant is a skull-mounted, wireless, rechargeable implant connected to electrode threads that are implanted in the brain by the R1 Robot, a robotic electrode thread inserter.
